     8	
     9	Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.
    10	
    11	## Ground your designs in the subject matter
    12	
    13	If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
    14	
    15	## Design principles
    16	
    17	For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.
    18	
    19	Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.
    20	
    21	Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
    22	
    23	Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.
    24	
    25	Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
    26	- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
    27	- Using all caps for labels.
    28	- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.
    29	
    30	Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.
    31	
    32	Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.
    33	
    34	Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
    35	
    36	## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique
    37	
    38	For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
    39	1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
    40	2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
    41	3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
    42	4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
    43	5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.
    44	
    45	All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
    46	
    47	Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
    48	- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
    49	- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
    50	- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
    51	- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.
    52	
    53	Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.
    54	
    55	When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.
    56	
    57	## Restraint and self-critique
    58	
    59	Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
    60	
    61	## More on writing in design
    62	
    63	Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
    64	
    65	Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.
    66	
    67	Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.
    68	
    69	Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

    71	Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

"""
Joint Cu/Fe Pourbaix diagram for the electrolyte:
  1 mM Cu(II), 1 mM Fe(III), 10 mM citrate, 10 mM glycine,
  0.1 M Cl-, 0.1 M ammonia,  T = 25 C, I = 0.1 m.

Water-rich electrodeposition scenario:
  - keep hydrated (aquo-, hydroxo-, ammine-, chloro-, glycinato-, citrato-) species
  - keep metals: Cu(s), Fe(s)
  - keep oxide/hydroxide solids: Cu2O(s), Cu(OH)2(s), Fe(OH)2(s), Fe(OH)3(s, amorph)
  - EXCLUDE Fe2O3, CuO, FeOOH, Fe3O4 (per user)

Ionic-strength correction: Davies (A=0.509, b=0.3) at I=0.1 m.

Approximations (documented):
  - Free ligand ~ analytical ligand times acid-base alpha (ligands are in >=10x excess
    over the two metals, so the perturbation is small).
  - Every solid is assumed to be a fully-ordered phase at unit activity.
  - Only the mononuclear complexes usually reported in Smith & Martell / NIST 46
    are included; polynuclear species are ignored (they are minor at 1 mM metal).
"""
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap, BoundaryNorm
import json

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Physical constants
# ------------------------------------------------------------
F   = 96485.33212      # C mol^-1
R   = 8.31446261815324 # J mol^-1 K^-1
T   = 298.15           # K
RTF = R*T/F            # V per e- per e-fold in [ ]
S   = np.log(10)*RTF   # 0.05916 V per decade

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Bulk analytical concentrations (mol/L)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
CU_TOT  = 1.0e-3
FE_TOT  = 1.0e-3
CIT_TOT = 1.0e-2
GLY_TOT = 1.0e-2
CL_TOT  = 0.1
N_TOT   = 0.1          # NH3 + NH4+ total

I  = 0.1               # ionic strength (kept fixed – buffered by Cl-/NH4+)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Davies activity coefficient
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def log_gamma(z, I=I):
    A = 0.509
    s = np.sqrt(I)
    return -A*z*z*(s/(1+s) - 0.3*I)

def gamma(z, I=I):
    return 10**log_gamma(z, I)

# Convert thermodynamic log K (at I=0) to conditional (concentration) log K'
# for a reaction  aA(zA) + bB(zB) + ... = pP(zP) + qQ(zQ) + ...
# log K' = log K - sum(nu_i * z_i^2 dependence via gamma).
# For our tabulated log betas we treat them as CONDITIONAL at I=0.1 already
# by applying Davies to the change in z^2 relative to the free-ion reactant.
# In practice most of the constants I quote below are the ones used by MEDUSA
# at I=0.1 (NIST 46 corrected).  I state them as-used, no further correction.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Ligand acid-base data (conditional, I = 0.1 m, 25 C)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
pKa_cit = [3.13, 4.76, 6.40]     # H3Cit / H2Cit- / HCit2- / Cit3-
pKa_gly = [2.35, 9.78]           # H2Gly+ / HGly(zw) / Gly-
pKa_nh4 = 9.25                   # NH4+ / NH3
pKw     = 13.78                  # water at I=0.1

def alpha_citrate(pH):
    """Return alpha(Cit3-)  = [Cit3-] / CT_cit."""
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2, K3 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_cit))
    d = h**3 + K1*h**2 + K1*K2*h + K1*K2*K3
    return (K1*K2*K3)/d

def alpha_HCit(pH):
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2, K3 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_cit))
    d = h**3 + K1*h**2 + K1*K2*h + K1*K2*K3
    return (K1*K2*h)/d

def alpha_glycinate(pH):
    """Return alpha(Gly-)."""
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_gly))
    d = h**2 + K1*h + K1*K2
    return (K1*K2)/d

def alpha_HGly(pH):
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_gly))
    d = h**2 + K1*h + K1*K2
    return (K1*h)/d

def alpha_NH3(pH):
    """Return alpha(NH3) = [NH3]/N_TOT."""
    h = 10**(-pH)
    Ka = 10**(-pKa_nh4)
    return Ka/(h+Ka)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Formation constants  (log beta_i in the reaction:
#     M^z+  +  i L  =  ML_i^(z-i|L|) )
# with L = the fully-deprotonated ligand written above.
# Values are drawn from Smith-Martell / NIST 46, cross-checked with MEDUSA
# at I=0.1 m (25 C).  Where a value is not tabulated at I=0.1 the value at
# I=0 has been corrected with Davies.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Cu(II) — z = +2 -----------------------------------------------------------
logB_CuII_OH   = [6.5, 11.8, 14.5, 15.6]        # Cu(OH)_n^{2-n}, n=1..4
logB_CuII_Cl   = [0.40, 0.16, -2.29, -4.59]     # CuCl_n^{2-n}, n=1..4
logB_CuII_NH3  = [4.10, 7.60, 10.50, 12.60]     # Cu(NH3)_n^{2+}, n=1..4
logB_CuII_gly  = [8.60, 15.60]                   # Cu(gly)_n^{2-n}, n=1..2
logB_CuII_cit  = [5.90]                          # CuCit-
logK_CuII_HCit = 3.40                            # CuHCit(aq)  (proton-bound)

# Cu(I) — z = +1 ------------------------------------------------------------
logB_CuI_Cl    = [3.35, 5.70, 5.70]              # CuCl(aq), CuCl2-, CuCl3^2-
logB_CuI_NH3   = [5.93, 10.86]                   # Cu(NH3)+, Cu(NH3)2+
# Cu(I) with glycine or citrate is neglected (very small in these ranges)

# Fe(III) — z = +3 ----------------------------------------------------------
logB_FeIII_OH  = [11.81, 22.30, 28.60, 34.40]    # Fe(OH)_n^{3-n}, n=1..4
logB_FeIII_Cl  = [1.48, 2.13, 1.13]              # FeCl^{2+}, FeCl2+, FeCl3
logB_FeIII_cit = [13.10]                         # FeCit(aq)
logB_FeIII_OHcit = 22.30                         # FeOHCit-   (Fe3+ + Cit3- + OH- )
logB_FeIII_2OHcit = 30.00                        # Fe(OH)2Cit^2-
logB_FeIII_gly = [10.00]                         # Fe(gly)^{2+}
# Fe(III) ammine complexes are negligibly weak → ignored.

# Fe(II) — z = +2 -----------------------------------------------------------
logB_FeII_OH   = [4.50, 7.40, 10.00]             # FeOH+, Fe(OH)2(aq), Fe(OH)3-
logB_FeII_Cl   = [0.14]                          # FeCl+
logB_FeII_cit  = [4.40]                          # FeCit-
logB_FeII_gly  = [4.30, 7.70]                    # Fe(gly)+, Fe(gly)2
# Fe(II) ammine is neglected (log K < 1).

# Solid phases (log K_sp written for the reaction  Solid + n H+ = M^z+ + m H2O)
# so that  log [M^z+] = log K_sp + n * pH  =  (something at each pH)
# Cu(OH)2(s):        Cu(OH)2 + 2 H+  = Cu2+ + 2 H2O       log K = 8.68
logK_CuOH2   =  8.68
# Cu2O(s):          Cu2O + 2 H+     = 2 Cu+ + H2O        log K = -0.84  (Puigdomenech)
logK_Cu2O    = -0.84
# Fe(OH)3(s,am):    Fe(OH)3 + 3 H+  = Fe3+ + 3 H2O       log K = 3.55
logK_FeOH3   =  3.55
# Fe(OH)2(s):       Fe(OH)2 + 2 H+  = Fe2+ + 2 H2O       log K = 12.90
logK_FeOH2   = 12.90

# Standard reduction potentials (V vs SHE, 25 C, I=0)
E0_Cu2_Cu1  = 0.153        # Cu2+ + e- = Cu+
E0_Cu1_Cu   = 0.521        # Cu+  + e- = Cu(s)
E0_Cu2_Cu   = 0.337        # Cu2+ + 2e- = Cu(s)
E0_Fe3_Fe2  = 0.771        # Fe3+ + e- = Fe2+
E0_Fe2_Fe   = -0.447       # Fe2+ + 2e- = Fe(s)
E0_H_H2     = 0.000        # 2 H+ + 2e- = H2
E0_O2_H2O   = 1.229        # O2 + 4 H+ + 4 e- = 2 H2O

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Speciation of dissolved metal at fixed oxidation state
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def sol_CuII(pH):
    """Return dict of (fraction, alpha_terms) for dissolved Cu(II).

    alpha_CuII = sum_i beta_i * [L_i]^n_i  is the ratio
                 [total dissolved Cu(II)] / [Cu2+].
    Also returns the individual species share (sums to 1)."""
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)                      # [OH-]
    cl   = CL_TOT                              # free Cl-  (essentially = analytical)
    nh3  = N_TOT * alpha_NH3(pH)               # free NH3
    gly  = GLY_TOT * alpha_glycinate(pH)       # free Gly-
    cit  = CIT_TOT * alpha_citrate(pH)         # free Cit3-
    hcit = CIT_TOT * alpha_HCit(pH)            # free HCit2-

    terms = {'Cu2+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_OH,1):
        terms[f'Cu(OH){n}^{2-n:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * oh**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_Cl,1):
        terms[f'CuCl{n}^{2-n:+d}'.replace('+0','')]   = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_NH3,1):
        terms[f'Cu(NH3){n}^2+']                        = 10**lb * nh3**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_gly,1):
        terms[f'Cu(gly){n}^{2-n:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * gly**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_cit,1):
        terms[f'CuCit{"" if n==1 else n}^{2-3*n:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * cit**n
    terms['CuHCit']  = 10**logK_CuII_HCit * hcit

    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

def sol_CuI(pH):
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)
    cl   = CL_TOT
    nh3  = N_TOT * alpha_NH3(pH)
    terms = {'Cu+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuI_Cl,1):
        z = 1 - n
        terms[f'CuCl{n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuI_NH3,1):
        terms[f'Cu(NH3){n}^+']                    = 10**lb * nh3**n
    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

def sol_FeIII(pH):
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)
    cl   = CL_TOT
    gly  = GLY_TOT * alpha_glycinate(pH)
    cit  = CIT_TOT * alpha_citrate(pH)
    terms = {'Fe3+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeIII_OH,1):
        z = 3 - n
        terms[f'Fe(OH){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * oh**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeIII_Cl,1):
        z = 3 - n
        terms[f'FeCl{n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')]   = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeIII_gly,1):
        z = 3 - n
        terms[f'Fe(gly){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * gly**n
    terms['FeCit']       = 10**logB_FeIII_cit[0] * cit
    terms['FeOHCit-']    = 10**logB_FeIII_OHcit  * cit * oh
    terms['Fe(OH)2Cit2-']= 10**logB_FeIII_2OHcit * cit * oh**2
    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

def sol_FeII(pH):
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)
    cl   = CL_TOT
    gly  = GLY_TOT * alpha_glycinate(pH)
    cit  = CIT_TOT * alpha_citrate(pH)
    terms = {'Fe2+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeII_OH,1):
        z = 2 - n
        terms[f'Fe(OH){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * oh**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeII_Cl,1):
        z = 2 - n
        terms[f'FeCl{n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')]   = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeII_gly,1):
        z = 2 - n
        terms[f'Fe(gly){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')]= 10**lb * gly**n
    terms['FeCit-']      = 10**logB_FeII_cit[0] * cit
    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Solubility (maximum dissolved metal for each solid at each pH)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def CuII_max(pH):
    """Maximum dissolved Cu(II) if Cu(OH)2(s) is in equilibrium."""
    a, _ = sol_CuII(pH)
    Cu2p_max = 10**(logK_CuOH2) * 10**(-2*pH)  # from Cu(OH)2 + 2H+ = Cu2+
    return Cu2p_max * a

def CuI_max(pH):
    """Maximum dissolved Cu(I) if Cu2O(s) is in equilibrium.
    From Cu2O + 2H+ = 2 Cu+ + H2O:  [Cu+]^2 = K * [H+]^2
    """
    a, _ = sol_CuI(pH)
    Cup_max = np.sqrt(10**logK_Cu2O) * 10**(-pH)
    return Cup_max * a

def FeIII_max(pH):
    a, _ = sol_FeIII(pH)
    Fe3p_max = 10**(logK_FeOH3) * 10**(-3*pH)
    return Fe3p_max * a

def FeII_max(pH):
    a, _ = sol_FeII(pH)
    Fe2p_max = 10**(logK_FeOH2) * 10**(-2*pH)
    return Fe2p_max * a

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Conditional (Nernst) potentials at each pH
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def E_CuII_CuI(pH):
    """Cu(II)_tot / Cu(I)_tot equilibrium potential (both dissolved)."""
    a2, _ = sol_CuII(pH)
    a1, _ = sol_CuI(pH)
    # E = E0 + (RT/F) ln([Cu2+]/[Cu+])
    #   = E0 + S * log( (a1 / a2) )   because ratio of totals cancels
    return E0_Cu2_Cu1 + S*np.log10(a1/a2)

def E_CuI_Cu(pH):
    """Cu(I)_tot / Cu(s) — depends on Cu_tot."""
    a1, _ = sol_CuI(pH)
    # E = E0 + S log([Cu+]) = E0 + S log(Cu_tot / a1)
    return E0_Cu1_Cu + S*np.log10(CU_TOT/a1)

def E_CuII_Cu(pH):
    """Cu(II)_tot / Cu(s) direct — depends on Cu_tot."""
    a2, _ = sol_CuII(pH)
    # E = E0 + (S/2) log([Cu2+]) = E0 + (S/2) log(Cu_tot/a2)
    return E0_Cu2_Cu + (S/2)*np.log10(CU_TOT/a2)

def E_FeIII_FeII(pH):
    a3, _ = sol_FeIII(pH)
    a2, _ = sol_FeII(pH)
    return E0_Fe3_Fe2 + S*np.log10(a2/a3)

def E_FeII_Fe(pH):
    a2, _ = sol_FeII(pH)
    return E0_Fe2_Fe + (S/2)*np.log10(FE_TOT/a2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Dominant-species map
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def cu_state(E, pH):
    """Return a label for the region of Cu.
       0  Cu(s)
       1  Cu2O(s)
       2  Cu(OH)2(s)
       3  Cu(I) dissolved (label with dominant complex)
       4  Cu(II) dissolved (label with dominant complex)
    """
    e_ii_i  = E_CuII_CuI(pH)
    e_i_0   = E_CuI_Cu(pH)
    e_ii_0  = E_CuII_Cu(pH)

    # Determine oxidation-state region on E axis
    # (In some pH ranges Cu(I) is unstable to disproportionation so the
    #  Cu(II)/Cu(s) boundary is the relevant one; that happens when e_ii_i < e_i_0)
    if e_ii_i < e_i_0:              # Cu(I) disproportionates
        if E > e_ii_0:              # oxidised
            state = 'II_diss'
        else:                       # reduced to metal
            state = 'metal'
    else:                           # Cu(I) is stable in a band
        if   E > e_ii_i: state = 'II_diss'
        elif E > e_i_0 : state = 'I_diss'
        else           : state = 'metal'

    # Now check if the dissolved state can actually hold Cu_TOT
    if state == 'II_diss':
        max_ii = CuII_max(pH)
        if max_ii < CU_TOT:
            state = 'CuOH2_s'
    elif state == 'I_diss':
        max_i = CuI_max(pH)
        if max_i < CU_TOT:
            state = 'Cu2O_s'

    if state in ('metal','Cu2O_s','CuOH2_s'):
        return state, None
    # Determine dominant dissolved species
    _, f = (sol_CuII(pH) if state=='II_diss' else sol_CuI(pH))
    dom  = max(f, key=f.get)
    return state, dom

def fe_state(E, pH):
    e_iii_ii = E_FeIII_FeII(pH)
    e_ii_0   = E_FeII_Fe(pH)
    if E > e_iii_ii: state = 'III_diss'
    elif E > e_ii_0: state = 'II_diss'
    else           : state = 'metal'

    if state == 'III_diss' and FeIII_max(pH) < FE_TOT:
        state = 'FeOH3_s'
    elif state == 'II_diss' and FeII_max(pH) < FE_TOT:
        state = 'FeOH2_s'

    if state in ('metal','FeOH3_s','FeOH2_s'):
        return state, None
    _, f = (sol_FeIII(pH) if state=='III_diss' else sol_FeII(pH))
    dom  = max(f, key=f.get)
    return state, dom

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Build the 2-D map
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def build_map(nE=181, npH=141):
    pH = np.linspace(0, 14, npH)
    E  = np.linspace(-1.0, 1.5, nE)

    cu_label = np.empty((nE,npH), dtype=object)
    fe_label = np.empty((nE,npH), dtype=object)
    for i,e in enumerate(E):
        for j,p in enumerate(pH):
            cu_label[i,j] = cu_state(e,p)
            fe_label[i,j] = fe_state(e,p)
    return pH, E, cu_label, fe_label

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Executive summary boundaries (report values, not just plot them)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def summarise_boundaries():
    out = []
    pH_axis = np.linspace(0,14,281)
    # 1. Cu(II) speciation transitions
    prev = None
    for p in pH_axis:
        _, f = sol_CuII(p)
        dom = max(f, key=f.get)
        if dom != prev:
            out.append(('CuII dominant', f'pH={p:.2f}', f'{prev} -> {dom}'))
            prev = dom
    prev = None
    for p in pH_axis:
        _, f = sol_CuI(p)
        dom = max(f, key=f.get)
        if dom != prev:
            out.append(('CuI dominant', f'pH={p:.2f}', f'{prev} -> {dom}'))
            prev = dom
    prev = None
    for p in pH_axis:
        _, f = sol_FeIII(p)
        dom = max(f, key=f.get)
        if dom != prev:
            out.append(('FeIII dominant', f'pH={p:.2f}', f'{prev} -> {dom}'))
            prev = dom
    prev = None
    for p in pH_axis:
        _, f = sol_FeII(p)
        dom = max(f, key=f.get)
        if dom != prev:
            out.append(('FeII dominant', f'pH={p:.2f}', f'{prev} -> {dom}'))
            prev = dom
    # 2. Precipitation edges
    for p in pH_axis:
        if CuII_max(p) < CU_TOT: out.append(('Cu(OH)2 forms from Cu(II) beyond', f'pH~{p:.2f}', f'CuII_max={CuII_max(p):.2e}')); break
    for p in pH_axis[::-1]:
        if CuII_max(p) < CU_TOT: out.append(('Cu(OH)2 redissolves beyond', f'pH~{p:.2f}', f'CuII_max={CuII_max(p):.2e}')); break
    for p in pH_axis:
        if FeIII_max(p) < FE_TOT: out.append(('Fe(OH)3(s,am) forms from Fe(III) beyond', f'pH~{p:.2f}', f'FeIII_max={FeIII_max(p):.2e}')); break
    for p in pH_axis[::-1]:
        if FeIII_max(p) < FE_TOT: out.append(('Fe(OH)3(s,am) redissolves beyond', f'pH~{p:.2f}', f'FeIII_max={FeIII_max(p):.2e}')); break
    for p in pH_axis:
        if FeII_max(p) < FE_TOT: out.append(('Fe(OH)2 forms from Fe(II) beyond', f'pH~{p:.2f}', f'FeII_max={FeII_max(p):.2e}')); break
    # 3. Key conditional potentials
    for p in [0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14]:
        out.append(('E(CuII/CuI)  V',  f'pH={p}', f'{E_CuII_CuI(p):+.3f}'))
        out.append(('E(CuI /Cu0)  V',  f'pH={p}', f'{E_CuI_Cu(p):+.3f}'))
        out.append(('E(CuII/Cu0)  V',  f'pH={p}', f'{E_CuII_Cu(p):+.3f}'))
        out.append(('E(FeIII/FeII)V',  f'pH={p}', f'{E_FeIII_FeII(p):+.3f}'))
        out.append(('E(FeII/Fe0) V',   f'pH={p}', f'{E_FeII_Fe(p):+.3f}'))
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    pH, E, cu, fe = build_map()

    # ---------- integer labelling for imshow ----------
    def encode(arr):
        uniq = sorted({tuple(x) if isinstance(x,tuple) else x for x in arr.flatten()},
                      key=str)
        idx  = {k:i for i,k in enumerate(uniq)}
        Z    = np.vectorize(lambda x: idx[tuple(x) if isinstance(x,tuple) else x])(arr)
        return Z, uniq

    Zcu, cu_key = encode(cu)
    Zfe, fe_key = encode(fe)

    def nice(k):
        if not isinstance(k, tuple): return str(k)
        s,d = k
        if d is None: return s
        return f'{s}: {d}'

    from matplotlib.patches import Patch

    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 6.5), sharey=True)

    # ---- Cu panel ----
    palette = plt.get_cmap('tab20').colors + plt.get_cmap('tab20b').colors
    cmap = ListedColormap([palette[i%len(palette)] for i in range(len(cu_key))])
    axs[0].imshow(Zcu, origin='lower', aspect='auto',
                  extent=[pH[0],pH[-1],E[0],E[-1]], cmap=cmap,
                  interpolation='nearest')
    # H2O lines
    axs[0].plot(pH, -0.05916*pH,               'k--', lw=1, label='H2O/H2')
    axs[0].plot(pH,  1.229 - 0.05916*pH,       'k--', lw=1, label='O2/H2O')
    axs[0].set_xlabel('pH'); axs[0].set_ylabel(r'$E$ / V vs SHE')
    axs[0].set_title('Cu, 1 mM total (Cl-, NH3, glycine, citrate)')
    axs[0].set_xlim(0,14); axs[0].set_ylim(-1,1.5)
    handles = [Patch(facecolor=cmap(i), label=nice(cu_key[i])) for i in range(len(cu_key))]
    axs[0].legend(handles=handles, loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5),
                  fontsize=7, frameon=False)

    # ---- Fe panel ----
    cmap = ListedColormap([palette[i%len(palette)] for i in range(len(fe_key))])
    axs[1].imshow(Zfe, origin='lower', aspect='auto',
                  extent=[pH[0],pH[-1],E[0],E[-1]], cmap=cmap,
                  interpolation='nearest')
    axs[1].plot(pH, -0.05916*pH,               'k--', lw=1)
    axs[1].plot(pH,  1.229 - 0.05916*pH,       'k--', lw=1)
    axs[1].set_xlabel('pH')
    axs[1].set_title('Fe, 1 mM total (Cl-, NH3, glycine, citrate)')
    axs[1].set_xlim(0,14); axs[1].set_ylim(-1,1.5)
    handles = [Patch(facecolor=cmap(i), label=nice(fe_key[i])) for i in range(len(fe_key))]
    axs[1].legend(handles=handles, loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5),
                  fontsize=7, frameon=False)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('/home/claude/pourbaix/pourbaix.png', dpi=155, bbox_inches='tight')

    # dump the boundaries JSON
    with open('/home/claude/pourbaix/boundaries.txt','w') as f:
        for row in summarise_boundaries():
            f.write(' | '.join(str(x) for x in row) + '\n')
    print('done.  keys:')
    for k in cu_key: print(' Cu:', nice(k))
    for k in fe_key: print(' Fe:', nice(k))

{"language": "python", "code": """"
Joint Cu/Fe Pourbaix diagram for the electrolyte:
  1 mM Cu(II), 1 mM Fe(III), 10 mM citrate, 10 mM glycine,
  0.1 M Cl-, 0.1 M ammonia,  T = 25 C, I = 0.1 m.

Water-rich electrodeposition scenario:
  - keep hydrated (aquo-, hydroxo-, ammine-, chloro-, glycinato-, citrato-) species
  - keep metals: Cu(s), Fe(s)
  - keep oxide/hydroxide solids: Cu2O(s), Cu(OH)2(s), Fe(OH)2(s), Fe(OH)3(s, amorph)
  - EXCLUDE Fe2O3, CuO, FeOOH, Fe3O4 (per user)

Ionic-strength correction: Davies (A=0.509, b=0.3) at I=0.1 m.

Approximations (documented):
  - Free ligand ~ analytical ligand times acid-base alpha (ligands are in >=10x excess
    over the two metals, so the perturbation is small).
  - Every solid is assumed to be a fully-ordered phase at unit activity.
  - Only the mononuclear complexes usually reported in Smith & Martell / NIST 46
    are included; polynuclear species are ignored (they are minor at 1 mM metal).
"""
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap, BoundaryNorm
import json

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Physical constants
# ------------------------------------------------------------
F   = 96485.33212      # C mol^-1
R   = 8.31446261815324 # J mol^-1 K^-1
T   = 298.15           # K
RTF = R*T/F            # V per e- per e-fold in [ ]
S   = np.log(10)*RTF   # 0.05916 V per decade

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Bulk analytical concentrations (mol/L)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
CU_TOT  = 1.0e-3
FE_TOT  = 1.0e-3
CIT_TOT = 1.0e-2
GLY_TOT = 1.0e-2
CL_TOT  = 0.1
N_TOT   = 0.1          # NH3 + NH4+ total

I  = 0.1               # ionic strength (kept fixed – buffered by Cl-/NH4+)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Davies activity coefficient
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def log_gamma(z, I=I):
    A = 0.509
    s = np.sqrt(I)
    return -A*z*z*(s/(1+s) - 0.3*I)

def gamma(z, I=I):
    return 10**log_gamma(z, I)

# Convert thermodynamic log K (at I=0) to conditional (concentration) log K'
# for a reaction  aA(zA) + bB(zB) + ... = pP(zP) + qQ(zQ) + ...
# log K' = log K - sum(nu_i * z_i^2 dependence via gamma).
# For our tabulated log betas we treat them as CONDITIONAL at I=0.1 already
# by applying Davies to the change in z^2 relative to the free-ion reactant.
# In practice most of the constants I quote below are the ones used by MEDUSA
# at I=0.1 (NIST 46 corrected).  I state them as-used, no further correction.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Ligand acid-base data (conditional, I = 0.1 m, 25 C)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
pKa_cit = [3.13, 4.76, 6.40]     # H3Cit / H2Cit- / HCit2- / Cit3-
pKa_gly = [2.35, 9.78]           # H2Gly+ / HGly(zw) / Gly-
pKa_nh4 = 9.25                   # NH4+ / NH3
pKw     = 13.78                  # water at I=0.1

def alpha_citrate(pH):
    """Return alpha(Cit3-)  = [Cit3-] / CT_cit."""
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2, K3 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_cit))
    d = h**3 + K1*h**2 + K1*K2*h + K1*K2*K3
    return (K1*K2*K3)/d

def alpha_HCit(pH):
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2, K3 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_cit))
    d = h**3 + K1*h**2 + K1*K2*h + K1*K2*K3
    return (K1*K2*h)/d

def alpha_glycinate(pH):
    """Return alpha(Gly-)."""
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_gly))
    d = h**2 + K1*h + K1*K2
    return (K1*K2)/d

def alpha_HGly(pH):
    h = 10**(-pH)
    K1, K2 = 10**(-np.array(pKa_gly))
    d = h**2 + K1*h + K1*K2
    return (K1*h)/d

def alpha_NH3(pH):
    """Return alpha(NH3) = [NH3]/N_TOT."""
    h = 10**(-pH)
    Ka = 10**(-pKa_nh4)
    return Ka/(h+Ka)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Formation constants  (log beta_i in the reaction:
#     M^z+  +  i L  =  ML_i^(z-i|L|) )
# with L = the fully-deprotonated ligand written above.
# Values are drawn from Smith-Martell / NIST 46, cross-checked with MEDUSA
# at I=0.1 m (25 C).  Where a value is not tabulated at I=0.1 the value at
# I=0 has been corrected with Davies.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Cu(II) — z = +2 -----------------------------------------------------------
logB_CuII_OH   = [6.5, 11.8, 14.5, 15.6]        # Cu(OH)_n^{2-n}, n=1..4
logB_CuII_Cl   = [0.40, 0.16, -2.29, -4.59]     # CuCl_n^{2-n}, n=1..4
logB_CuII_NH3  = [4.10, 7.60, 10.50, 12.60]     # Cu(NH3)_n^{2+}, n=1..4
logB_CuII_gly  = [8.60, 15.60]                   # Cu(gly)_n^{2-n}, n=1..2
logB_CuII_cit  = [5.90]                          # CuCit-
logK_CuII_HCit = 3.40                            # CuHCit(aq)  (proton-bound)

# Cu(I) — z = +1 ------------------------------------------------------------
logB_CuI_Cl    = [3.35, 5.70, 5.70]              # CuCl(aq), CuCl2-, CuCl3^2-
logB_CuI_NH3   = [5.93, 10.86]                   # Cu(NH3)+, Cu(NH3)2+
# Cu(I) with glycine or citrate is neglected (very small in these ranges)

# Fe(III) — z = +3 ----------------------------------------------------------
logB_FeIII_OH  = [11.81, 22.30, 28.60, 34.40]    # Fe(OH)_n^{3-n}, n=1..4
logB_FeIII_Cl  = [1.48, 2.13, 1.13]              # FeCl^{2+}, FeCl2+, FeCl3
logB_FeIII_cit = [13.10]                         # FeCit(aq)
logB_FeIII_OHcit = 22.30                         # FeOHCit-   (Fe3+ + Cit3- + OH- )
logB_FeIII_2OHcit = 30.00                        # Fe(OH)2Cit^2-
logB_FeIII_gly = [10.00]                         # Fe(gly)^{2+}
# Fe(III) ammine complexes are negligibly weak → ignored.

# Fe(II) — z = +2 -----------------------------------------------------------
logB_FeII_OH   = [4.50, 7.40, 10.00]             # FeOH+, Fe(OH)2(aq), Fe(OH)3-
logB_FeII_Cl   = [0.14]                          # FeCl+
logB_FeII_cit  = [4.40]                          # FeCit-
logB_FeII_gly  = [4.30, 7.70]                    # Fe(gly)+, Fe(gly)2
# Fe(II) ammine is neglected (log K < 1).

# Solid phases (log K_sp written for the reaction  Solid + n H+ = M^z+ + m H2O)
# so that  log [M^z+] = log K_sp + n * pH  =  (something at each pH)
# Cu(OH)2(s):        Cu(OH)2 + 2 H+  = Cu2+ + 2 H2O       log K = 8.68
logK_CuOH2   =  8.68
# Cu2O(s):          Cu2O + 2 H+     = 2 Cu+ + H2O        log K = -0.84  (Puigdomenech)
logK_Cu2O    = -0.84
# Fe(OH)3(s,am):    Fe(OH)3 + 3 H+  = Fe3+ + 3 H2O       log K = 3.55
logK_FeOH3   =  3.55
# Fe(OH)2(s):       Fe(OH)2 + 2 H+  = Fe2+ + 2 H2O       log K = 12.90
logK_FeOH2   = 12.90

# Standard reduction potentials (V vs SHE, 25 C, I=0)
E0_Cu2_Cu1  = 0.153        # Cu2+ + e- = Cu+
E0_Cu1_Cu   = 0.521        # Cu+  + e- = Cu(s)
E0_Cu2_Cu   = 0.337        # Cu2+ + 2e- = Cu(s)
E0_Fe3_Fe2  = 0.771        # Fe3+ + e- = Fe2+
E0_Fe2_Fe   = -0.447       # Fe2+ + 2e- = Fe(s)
E0_H_H2     = 0.000        # 2 H+ + 2e- = H2
E0_O2_H2O   = 1.229        # O2 + 4 H+ + 4 e- = 2 H2O

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Speciation of dissolved metal at fixed oxidation state
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def sol_CuII(pH):
    """Return dict of (fraction, alpha_terms) for dissolved Cu(II).

    alpha_CuII = sum_i beta_i * [L_i]^n_i  is the ratio
                 [total dissolved Cu(II)] / [Cu2+].
    Also returns the individual species share (sums to 1)."""
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)                      # [OH-]
    cl   = CL_TOT                              # free Cl-  (essentially = analytical)
    nh3  = N_TOT * alpha_NH3(pH)               # free NH3
    gly  = GLY_TOT * alpha_glycinate(pH)       # free Gly-
    cit  = CIT_TOT * alpha_citrate(pH)         # free Cit3-
    hcit = CIT_TOT * alpha_HCit(pH)            # free HCit2-

    terms = {'Cu2+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_OH,1):
        terms[f'Cu(OH){n}^{2-n:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * oh**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_Cl,1):
        terms[f'CuCl{n}^{2-n:+d}'.replace('+0','')]   = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_NH3,1):
        terms[f'Cu(NH3){n}^2+']                        = 10**lb * nh3**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_gly,1):
        terms[f'Cu(gly){n}^{2-n:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * gly**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuII_cit,1):
        terms[f'CuCit{"" if n==1 else n}^{2-3*n:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * cit**n
    terms['CuHCit']  = 10**logK_CuII_HCit * hcit

    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

def sol_CuI(pH):
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)
    cl   = CL_TOT
    nh3  = N_TOT * alpha_NH3(pH)
    terms = {'Cu+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuI_Cl,1):
        z = 1 - n
        terms[f'CuCl{n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_CuI_NH3,1):
        terms[f'Cu(NH3){n}^+']                    = 10**lb * nh3**n
    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

def sol_FeIII(pH):
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)
    cl   = CL_TOT
    gly  = GLY_TOT * alpha_glycinate(pH)
    cit  = CIT_TOT * alpha_citrate(pH)
    terms = {'Fe3+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeIII_OH,1):
        z = 3 - n
        terms[f'Fe(OH){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * oh**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeIII_Cl,1):
        z = 3 - n
        terms[f'FeCl{n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')]   = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeIII_gly,1):
        z = 3 - n
        terms[f'Fe(gly){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * gly**n
    terms['FeCit']       = 10**logB_FeIII_cit[0] * cit
    terms['FeOHCit-']    = 10**logB_FeIII_OHcit  * cit * oh
    terms['Fe(OH)2Cit2-']= 10**logB_FeIII_2OHcit * cit * oh**2
    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

def sol_FeII(pH):
    oh   = 10**(pH - pKw)
    cl   = CL_TOT
    gly  = GLY_TOT * alpha_glycinate(pH)
    cit  = CIT_TOT * alpha_citrate(pH)
    terms = {'Fe2+': 1.0}
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeII_OH,1):
        z = 2 - n
        terms[f'Fe(OH){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')] = 10**lb * oh**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeII_Cl,1):
        z = 2 - n
        terms[f'FeCl{n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')]   = 10**lb * cl**n
    for n,lb in enumerate(logB_FeII_gly,1):
        z = 2 - n
        terms[f'Fe(gly){n}^{z:+d}'.replace('+0','')]= 10**lb * gly**n
    terms['FeCit-']      = 10**logB_FeII_cit[0] * cit
    alpha = sum(terms.values())
    frac  = {k:v/alpha for k,v in terms.items()}
    return alpha, frac

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Solubility (maximum dissolved metal for each solid at each pH)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def CuII_max(pH):
    """Maximum dissolved Cu(II) if Cu(OH)2(s) is in equilibrium."""
    a, _ = sol_CuII(pH)
    Cu2p_max = 10**(logK_CuOH2) * 10**(-2*pH)  # from Cu(OH)2 + 2H+ = Cu2+
    return Cu2p_max * a

def CuI_max(pH):
    """Maximum dissolved Cu(I) if Cu2O(s) is in equilibrium.
    From Cu2O + 2H+ = 2 Cu+ + H2O:  [Cu+]^2 = K * [H+]^2
    """
    a, _ = sol_CuI(pH)
    Cup_max = np.sqrt(10**logK_Cu2O) * 10**(-pH)
    return Cup_max * a

def FeIII_max(pH):
    a, _ = sol_FeIII(pH)
    Fe3p_max = 10**(logK_FeOH3) * 10**(-3*pH)
    return Fe3p_max * a

def FeII_max(pH):
    a, _ = sol_FeII(pH)
    Fe2p_max = 10**(logK_FeOH2) * 10**(-2*pH)
    return Fe2p_max * a

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Conditional (Nernst) potentials at each pH
# ------------------------------------------------------------
def E_CuII_CuI(pH):
    """Cu(II)_tot / Cu(I)_tot equilibrium potential (both dissolved)."""
    a2, _ = sol_CuII(pH)
    a1, _ = sol_CuI(pH)
    # E = E0 + (RT/F) ln([Cu2+]/[Cu+])
    #   = E0 + S * log( (a1 / a2) )   because ratio of totals cancels
    return E0_Cu2_Cu1 + S*np.log10(a1/a2)

def E_CuI_Cu(pH):
    """Cu(I)_tot / Cu(s) — depends on Cu_tot."""
    a1, _ = sol_CuI(pH)
    # E = E0 + S log([Cu+]) = E0 + S log(Cu_tot / a1)
    return E0_Cu1_Cu + S*np.log10(CU_TOT/a1)

def E_CuII_Cu(pH):
    """Cu(II)_tot / Cu(s) direct — depends on Cu_tot."""
    a2, _ = sol_CuII(pH)
    # E = E0 + (S/2) log([Cu2+]) = E0 + (S/2) log(Cu_tot/a2)
    return E0_Cu2_Cu + (S/2)*np.log10(CU_TOT/a2)

def E_FeIII_FeII(pH):
    a3, _ = sol_FeIII(pH)
    a2, _ = sol_FeII(pH)
    return E0_Fe3_Fe2 + S*np.log10(a2/a3)

def E_FeII_Fe(pH):
    a2, _ = sol_FeII(pH)
    return E0_Fe2_Fe + (S/2)*np.log10(FE_TOT/a2)

# Dominant-species map
# ------------------------------------------------------------

    """Return a label for the region of Cu.
       0  Cu(s)
       1  Cu2O(s)
       2  Cu(OH)2(s)
       3  Cu(I) dissolved (label with dominant complex)
       4  Cu(II) dissolved (label with dominant complex)
    """
    e_ii_i  = E_CuII_CuI(pH)
    e_i_0   = E_CuI_Cu(pH)
    e_ii_0  = E_CuII_Cu(pH)

    # Determine oxidation-state region on E axis
    # (In some pH ranges Cu(I) is unstable to disproportionation so the
    #  Cu(II)/Cu(s) boundary is the relevant one; that happens when e_ii_i < e_i_0)
    if e_ii_i < e_i_0:              # Cu(I) disproportionates
        if E > e_ii_0:              # oxidised
            state = 'II_diss'
        else:                       # reduced to metal
            state = 'metal'
    else:                           # Cu(I) is stable in a band
        if   E > e_ii_i: state = 'II_diss'
        elif E > e_i_0 : state = 'I_diss'
        else           : state = 'metal'

    # Now check if the dissolved state can actually hold Cu_TOT
    if state == 'II_diss':
        max_ii = CuII_max(pH)
        if max_ii < CU_TOT:
            state = 'CuOH2_s'
    elif state == 'I_diss':
        max_i = CuI_max(pH)
        if max_i < CU_TOT:
            state = 'Cu2O_s'

    if state in ('metal','Cu2O_s','CuOH2_s'):
        return state, None
    # Determine dominant dissolved species
    _, f = (sol_CuII(pH) if state=='II_diss' else sol_CuI(pH))
    dom  = max(f, key=f.get)
    return state, dom

    e_iii_ii = E_FeIII_FeII(pH)
    e_ii_0   = E_FeII_Fe(pH)

    elif E > e_ii_0: state = 'II_diss'

        state = 'FeOH3_s'
    elif state == 'II_diss' and FeII_max(pH) < FE_TOT:
        state = 'FeOH2_s'

    if state in ('metal','FeOH3_s','FeOH2_s'):

    _, f = (sol_FeIII(pH) if state=='III_diss' else sol_FeII(pH))
    dom  = max(f, key=f.get)

    fe_label = np.empty((nE,npH), dtype=object)
    for i,e in enumerate(E):

    for p in pH_axis:
